headline: Five long-unseen paintings unveiled in ‘almost mythical’ sale of private collection – video

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Sotheby's has revealed five paintings from Cézanne, Renoir, Monet and De Vlaminck as part of the Blaquier-Arrieta Collection, which is expected to fetch approximately $450m when it goes on sale in New York in November. The rest of the collection is being showcased digitally, including Vincent van Gogh’s Châtaigniers en fleurs. Most of the paintings were acquired in London in the 1970s by Carlos Pedro Blaquier and Nelly Blaquier de Arrieta. Continue reading...
sources.title: Five long-unseen paintings unveiled in ‘almost mythical’ sale of private collection – video

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Châtaigniers en fleurs, valued at $180m, to be auctioned along with 11 other works by likes of Cézanne and Monet For more than 50 years it was held in a private art collection with an “almost mythical status” that was likened to a miniature version of Paris’s Musée d’Orsay. But a painting by Vincent van Gogh created during the last two months of his life will go on display this month before being put up for auction with a value of $180m (£136m). Continue reading...
sources.title: Van Gogh to go on display before sale of ‘almost mythical’ private collection
